'''Rudy Lee Horne''' (1968 – 2017) was an American mathematician and professor of mathematics at [[Morehouse College]]. He worked on [[dynamical system]]s, including [[nonlinear system|nonlinear]] waves. He was the mathematics consultant for the film ''[[Hidden Figures]]''.<ref name=":0" />

== Early life and education ==
Horne grew up in the [[south side of Chicago]].<ref name=":1"/> His father worked at [[Sherwin-Williams]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|url=http://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/rudy-horne/|title=Rudy L. Horne, Jr. - Mathematically Gifted & Black|work=Mathematically Gifted & Black|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en-US}}</ref> He graduated from [[Crete-Monee High School]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/rudy-l-horne-dies-at-49-chicago-native-checked-the-math-in-hidden-figures-2/|title=Rudy L. Horne dies at 49; Chicago native checked the math in 'Hidden Figures'|work=Chicago Sun-Times|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cm201u.org/index.aspx?NID=4927|title=Crete-Monee School District, IL - CMMS Celebrates Black History Month|website=www.cm201u.org|language=en|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref> He completed a [[double degree]] in mathematics and physics at the [[University of Oklahoma]] in 1991.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ou.edu/admissions/sooner-stories/math-movies-and-ou|title=Math, Movies and OU|website=www.ou.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://www.kgou.org/post/ou-graduate-makes-sure-hidden-figures-math-adds|title=OU Graduate Makes Sure "Hidden Figures" Math Adds Up|last=McCleland|first=Jacob|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en}}</ref> He joined the [[University of Colorado Boulder]] for his postgraduate studies, earning a master's in physics in 1994 and in mathematics in 1996. He completed his doctorate, ''Collision induced timing jitter and four-wave mixing in wavelength division multiplexing soliton systems'', in 2001 which was supervised by [[Mark J. Ablowitz]].<ref name=mathgene/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/horne_rudy2.html|title=Rudy Horne, Jr. - Mathematician of the African Diaspora|website=www.math.buffalo.edu|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref> He was the first African American to graduate from the [[University of Colorado Boulder]] Department of Applied Mathematics.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.colorado.edu/amath/2017/12/21/honoring-dr-rudy-horne|title=Honoring Dr. Rudy Horne|date=2017-12-21|work=Applied Mathematics|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en}}</ref>

== Career and research==
After completing his PhD, Horne had a position at the [[California State University, East Bay]].<ref name=":0" />  before working as [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], with Chris Jones.<ref name="Systems">{{Cite news|url=https://dsweb.siam.org/The-Magazine/Article/in-memoriam-rudy-l-horne|title=In Memoriam: Rudy L. Horne|work=Dynamical Systems|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en-US}}</ref> Horne joined [[Florida State University]] in 2005.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.fsu.edu/People/faculty.php?id=641|title=Rudy Horne's Math Page|website=www.math.fsu.edu|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref> Horne joined [[Morehouse College]] in 2010 and was promoted to associate professor of mathematics in 2015.<ref name=":0" /> He continued to study [[four-wave mixing]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Horne|first1=Rudy L.|last2=Jones|first2=Christopher K. R. T.|last3=Schäfer|first3=Tobias|date=2008|title=The Suppression of Four-Wave Mixing by Random Dispersion|journal=SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics|volume=69|issue=3|pages=690–703|jstor=40233639|doi=10.1137/070680539}}</ref> His work considered nonlinear optical phenomena.<ref name="Systems"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dam.brown.edu/people/sandsted/conferences/gmids-11/talks/horne.pdf|title=Geometric methods and optical phenomena: Wave stability in certain optical devices|last=Horne|first=Rudy L.|date=2011-05-11|website=Brown|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180910014659/http://www.dam.brown.edu/people/sandsted/conferences/gmids-11/talks/horne.pdf|archive-date=2018-09-10|url-status=dead|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm2013/2141_program_saturday.html|title=Joint Mathematics Meetings|website=jointmathematicsmeetings.org|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref> He uncovered effects in [[Parity-time symmetry|parity-time symmetric systems]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://math.unc.edu/2017/12/rudy-hornes-passing/|title=Rudy Horne's Passing {{!}} Department of Mathematics|website=math.unc.edu|language=en-US|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>

Horne was recommended to serve as a mathematics consultant for [[Hidden Figures]] by [[Morehouse College]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nist.gov/blogs/taking-measure/plotting-path-nasa-grids-nist-graphics|title=Plotting a Path from NASA Grids to NIST Graphics|last=Esser|first=Mark|date=2017-04-27|work=NIST|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sciencenewsforstudents.org/article/meet-people-behind-film-hidden-figures|title=Meet the people behind the film Hidden Figures|last=Miller|first=Gerri|date=2018-06-20|work=Science News for Students|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en}}</ref> He worked closely with [[Theodore Melfi]] ensured the actors knew how to pronounce "Euler's".<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/publications/journals/notices/201706/rnoti-p620.pdf|title=Hidden Figures|last=Hunt|first=Fern|date=2017|website=AMS|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.insidescience.org/news/exploring-math-hidden-figures|title=Exploring the Math in 'Hidden Figures'|date=2017-02-24|work=Inside Science|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.american.edu/ucm/news/20170223-Jackson-math.cfm|title=Being Counted: Professor Talks 'Hidden Figures' and Minority Women in Math {{!}} American University Washington D.C.|website=American University|date=23 February 2017 |language=en-US|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://issuu.com/morehousemagazine/docs/morehouse_magazine_150th_final/14|title=Morehouse Magazine Special Anniversary Issue|work=Issuu|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bfi.org.uk/films-tv-people/588fe2a93afbb|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180704151558/http://www.bfi.org.uk/films-tv-people/588fe2a93afbb|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 4, 2018|title=Rudy L. Horne {{!}} BFI|website=www.bfi.org.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref> He spent four months working with [[20th Century Fox]].<ref name=":2" /> In particular, Horne worked with [[Taraji P. Henson]] on the mathematics she required for her role as [[Katherine Johnson]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://dose.com/articles/this-hidden-figures-mathematician-inspired-generations-of-black-students/|title=This "Hidden Figures" Mathematician Inspired Generations Of Black Students|date=2018-01-26|work=dose.|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.producersguild.org/blogpost/1537650/264534/DO-THE-MATH--An-Amazing-True-Story-Plus-A-Dedicated-Team-Adds-Up-To-Hidden-Figures|title=DO THE MATH - An Amazing True Story Plus A Dedicated Team Adds Up To "Hidden Figures" - Producers Guild of America|website=www.producersguild.org|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref> He taught the cast how to get excited by mathematics.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.space.com/33886-hidden-figures-movie-set-visit.html|title=On 'Hidden Figures' Set, NASA's Early Years Take Center Stage|work=Space.com|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref> His handwriting is on screen during a scene at the beginning of the film where [[Katherine Johnson]] solves a quadratic equation.<ref name=":1" /> He appeared on the interview series ''In the Know.''<ref>{{Citation|last=In The Know|title=In The Know: Meet Dr. Rudy Horne|date=2017-08-14|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y72ant_6nsI|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref> Horne completed a [[Mathematical Association of America]] ''Maths Fest'' tour where he discussed the mathematics in [[Hidden Figures]], focusing on the calculations that concerned Glenn's orbit around the Earth in 1962.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/meetings/mathfest/program-details/2017/invited-addresses|title=Invited Addresses {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|language=en|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mcaim.math.lsa.umich.edu/event/dr-marjorie-lee-browne-colloquium-as-part-of-the-university-of-michigans-rev-dr-martin-luther-king-jr-symposium-professor-rudy-horne-associate-professor-of-mathematics-morehouse-college/|title=Hidden Figures: Bringing Math, Physics, History, and Race to Hollywood -Free Movie Screening, Colloquium & Reception {{!}} MCAIM|website=mcaim.math.lsa.umich.edu|language=en-US|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref> He appeared on [[NPR]]'s Closer Look.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wabe.org/episode/closer-look-hidden-figures-women-hip-hop-and-more/|title=Closer Look: 'Hidden Figures'; Women In Hip-Hop; And More {{!}} 90.1 FM WABE|work=90.1 FM WABE|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en-US}}</ref>

He died on December 11, 2017, after surgery for a torn [[aorta]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.morehouse.edu/newscenter/morehousecollegemournsthelossofdrrudyhorne.html|title=Morehouse College {{!}} House News|last=College|first=Morehouse|website=www.morehouse.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/news/memoriam|title=In Memoriam {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|language=en|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> The [[University of Colorado Boulder]] established a Rudy Lee Horne Memorial Fellowship in his honour.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://giving.cu.edu/fund/rudy-lee-horne-endowed-graduate-fellowship-applied-mathematics-fund|title=Rudy Lee Horne Endowed Graduate Fellowship in Applied Mathematics Fund {{!}} CU Boulder {{!}} Giving to CU|website=giving.cu.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref> He was described as a "rock star", inspiring generations of black students.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.blackengineer.com/article/rudy-horne-math-rock-star-remembered/|title=Rudy Horne: Math rock star remembered - US Black Engineer|work=US Black Engineer|access-date=2018-09-09|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> He was awarded the [[National Association of Mathematicians]] (NAM) lifetime achievement award posthumously in 2018,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lifetime Achievement Award|url=https://www.nam-math.org/lifetime-achievement.html|access-date=2018-09-09|website=www.nam-math.org|language=en}}</ref> and was recognized by [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] as a Black History Month 2018 Honoree.<ref name=":4" />
